title: Live stream: a position is the JMAP Message state string; Subscribe replays Message/changes
description:
Epic mimid-e64f; docs/design/binary-live-stream.md §5.5, §9 question 4; findings log F1.

Chosen (Mark, 2026-11-20): a stream position is the JMAP Message state string. The agent keeps no new kind of state; JMAP catch-up and the stream meet at one value.

Subscribe semantics, chosen by the agent for mimid-e64f (INVENTED, NOT FROM SPEC):
- Subscribe with since: the provider sends a Deliver for each Message that Message/changes from since and Message/get of the ids return, in that order, then answers the Subscribe with an Ack whose state covers them.
- Subscribe without since: every stored Message, as Message/get with ids null.
- Live: on each change-bus event the provider runs the same Message/changes and Message/get from the last state it sent, sends the Delivers, then Position with the new state. A lagging bus loses nothing; changes come from the store.
- cannotResume only when since does not parse or is ahead of the current state; the agent then subscribes without since, as it falls back on cannotCalculateChanges.
- One Subscribe per connection; a second is badMessage.
- Position exists because the state s.m is not one counter (F1): positions are sparse and the agent keeps its handled list between them, as on JMAP.
close_reason: Decided by Mark 2026-11-20 (mimid-e64f); details marked INVENTED chosen by agent, unattended
